5. **Phase A gates:** the first eight entries of §Test Commands (formatter, linter, the agent crate, the root bin, the
   canary binary, then `run --unit`, `run --integration`, `run --e2e`), all green before phase B — read green by the
   stopped run; not re-fired in Revision 1.

8. **The sender's compiled texts and Run B's literal** (`ledger.rs`, beside `PROBE_PROMPT` and `DIALOG_SETTINGS`
   (ledger.rs:320); `(security-plan · decision/probe-prompts-synthetic)`):
   - `CROSS_SESSION_TEXT` — synthetic ASCII saying what it is: «viola verify probe: a synthetic cross-session message
     sent by viola verify; reply with the single word ok»;
   - **[Revision 1]** `uds_address(runtime: &OsStr, pid: u32) -> Option<String>`, pure, in the Claude adapter crate.
     It returns `uds:` + runtime + `/cc-socks/` + pid + `.sock`, the form 2.1.328 names its own inbox socket
     (research `## Revision 1`).
     - It returns `None` when the runtime value is not absolute, holds a `.` or `..` component, or holds a byte
       outside `[A-Za-z0-9/._-]`. Those refusals keep a C0, C1, DEL or space out of a prompt; nothing is stripped.
     - It also returns `None` when the composed path, without `uds:`, is over 103 bytes (the CLI's own bound, past
       which it names its socket elsewhere).
     - One trailing `/` of the runtime value is dropped, as the CLI's path join does.
     - Compiled literals beside `SETTINGS_FLAG`: `UDS_SCHEME` (`uds:`), `CLI_SOCKET_DIR` (`cc-socks`),
       `CLI_SOCKET_SUFFIX` (`.sock`), `CLI_SOCKET_PATH_MAX` (103). Each is a reading of the 2.1.328 bundle. It is a
       premise the row's own probe measures, not a ledger row of its own: a CLI that names its socket otherwise reads
       the start red (the connect finds nothing, `send` · `refused`), never a false pass (`inputs#I8` item 1).
   - `sender_prompt(address)` = `CROSS_SESSION_SENDER_HEAD` + address + `CROSS_SESSION_SENDER_TAIL`: one `SendMessage`
     call with `to` the address that follows, the message `CROSS_SESSION_TEXT`, then the single word ok. **[Revision 1]**
     The head now reads «… with to set to exactly this address: » in place of «… to the session id ». The address must
     open with `UDS_SCHEME` and pass `uds_address`'s byte set, else `None`. The bare session id leaves the prompt
     (`inputs#I8` item 3);
   - `CROSS_SESSION_SETTINGS` = `{"crossSessionInbound":"accept"}`, Run B's only settings document;
   - `ALLOWED_TOOLS_FLAG` = `--allowedTools` beside the flag literals.

9. **`TypedRun.cross_session: Option<CrossSessionRun>`**: `prompts_before`, `sender` (`Exited` · `Failed` ·
   `Deadline`), `latency_ms`, and from the sender's `Tool.*.json` files in `k` order (each read through
   `take(MAX_FRAME)`): `sender_tools` (the `pre` files' words, in first-seen order, deduped; `none` when no file) and
   `send_result` (the `post` file's word; `none` when no `post` file stands — a send whose input failed validation
   fires none). **`ledger::cross_session_reading(trusted, typed)`** gives the outcome word and the prefix id:
   `not-run` · `sender-failed` · `sender-deadline` · `no-prompt` (no UserPromptSubmit past `prompts_before`) ·
   `unprefixed` (its `harness_prefix` is `None`) · `harness`. The row passes on `harness` alone; `sender_tools` and
   `send_result` decide nothing. As built (the stopped run's note 5): `sender_tools` / `send_result` stamp the string
   `none` where no file stood, `null` where the sender never started. **[Revision 1]** `not-run` also covers «no
   address composed» (step 11): no sender started, so both read `null`.

11. **Run B's cross-session turn** (`src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs`, `turns.rs`, `typed.rs`):
    - **Run B's args** (`trusted_args`, runs.rs:104): the run's args, then `SETTINGS_FLAG` + `CROSS_SESSION_SETTINGS`,
      then the plugin dir — `dialog_run`'s form (runs.rs:122).
    - **Where:** between the `/compact` paste's answer and the `/clear` paste (lean T1, standing), only when the box
      guard reads the box up. **[Revision 1]** The gate is no longer `ledger::resume_target`; the id is not used here,
      though Run E keeps it. The turn needs two things:
      - `Run::child_pid` (`src/cmd/verify/typed/run.rs:247`) gives Run B's pid;
      - `ledger::uds_address(inputs.runtime_dir, pid)` composes the address.
      With either missing, no sender is spawned and the reading is `not-run`. The address is composed from verify's own
      live child: no directory read, no `stat`, no listing, no name, nothing read of the roster or of the peer key
      (`inputs#I8` items 1, 3, 5). The CLI's connect does its own checks: a usable local path, no symlink at the path,
      a 5 s timeout.
    - **The sender:** `run_bounded` with subject `verify-sender`: `program_args` + `-p <sender_prompt(address)> --model haiku
      --no-session-persistence --allowedTools SendMessage --plugin-dir <sender plugin>`, no `--settings`; cwd the print
      probe's `ProbeDir` (`Inputs` gains `sender_cwd` and `sender: RunDirs`, typed.rs:59); the sender plugin and its
      0700 captures dir inside it, written by `write_plugin` with `ProbePlugin::Sender`; the same R8 strip; bound
      `SENDER_DEADLINE` (120 s, beside `PROBE_DEADLINE`, verify.rs:45); stopped by the stop.
    - **The wait:** on exit 0, one more UserPromptSubmit up to `CROSS_SESSION_WINDOW` (30 s), then its turn's end up to
      the probe deadline; a non-zero exit or the deadline skips the wait. No retry inside one verify.
    - **After it:** the box guard re-read; up → `/clear` pasted and Run B ends by Ctrl-C as today; not up → no
      `/clear`, Run B ends by `end_by_kill`, no key (lean T2; `(architecture · decision/verify-types-nothing-into-dialogs)`).

12. **`src/cmd/verify.rs`:** `measure` passes the sender inputs; `check_rows` checks 29 rows; `SENDER_DEADLINE`.
    **[Revision 1, held behind fork X1 — option (a), recommended]:**
    - `measure` reads `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` ONCE, at its start, through `std::env::var_os`. This is the value Run B
      inherits: the R8 strip removes only `CLAUDE*` names (`plan_strip`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs:76-96`),
      and the rig's `VR` arm keeps the real one for verify (`crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs:31`).
    - The value goes into `Inputs.runtime_dir: Option<&OsStr>` (`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs`). It is held in memory and
      used only by step 11's composition.
    - It reaches the sender's argv alone, and through it the sender's prompt to the model. It reaches no log line,
      stamp, fixture, error or step line. It configures nothing.
    - With it absent, or refused by `uds_address`, no sender is spawned and the row reads `fail` (`not-run`).
    - Its doc comment names the operator's ratification (`inputs#I8` item 1) and the Decisions Log entry X1's answer
      makes.
    - The word at P5 answers X1. An answer of (b) re-plans this step and step 14 before `XS-2`: the composition takes
      `/run/user/<euid>` from `libc::geteuid`, and no env read is added.
    **`schemas/diag-line.v1.json`** adds `verify-sender` to the `subject` enum (obs S2), `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs`
    its case.

13. **The fake agent** (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/agents.rs`,
    `test_cases_modes.rs`; fake-agent only; arch S3):
    - **Sender:** a `-p` prompt opening `CROSS_SESSION_SENDER_HEAD` is a sender. **[Revision 1]** It resolves its
      target by the uds address it is given (`inputs#I8` item 9). It reads the address, which must open with
      `UDS_SCHEME` and end `/cc-socks/<pid>.sock` under an absolute dir. The `<pid>` must be a live process whose
      parent pid equals the sender's own parent pid, read from `/proc/<pid>/stat` (`agents::parent_of`,
      `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/agents.rs:134`). That process's receiver must listen: `<exe dir>/inbox/<pid>.listening`
      stands (the stopped run's deviation 1, folded). The registry lookup by `sessionId`
      (`agents::sibling_session`, agents.rs:125) is replaced by that pid check. The fake reads no environment
      variable; the composition from the runtime dir is pinned by step 14's argv assertion.
      Then it runs its `--plugin-dir`'s PreToolUse then PostToolUse hooks with SYNTHETIC compiled payloads
      (`tool_name` `SendMessage`, `tool_input.to` the address, a `tool_response` of `{"success":true}`; named synthetic,
      `(test-plan · decision/synthetic-fixture-text)`), writes an empty 0600 `<exe dir>/inbox/<that pid>` and exits 0.
      It exits 1, with nothing written and no hook run, when the address is not of that shape, the pid is no listening
      sibling, or the set holds no `UserPromptSubmit.cross-session-1.json`.
    - **Receiver:** under `--framing`, an interactive fake polls its own inbox file only when its argv carries
      `--settings` equal to `CROSS_SESSION_SETTINGS`; on the file it removes it, fires `UserPromptSubmit` variant
      `cross-session-1` as recorded, then ends the turn.
    - **`--cross-session-turn-screen <phase>`**, parsed beside `--tag-turn-screen`, for step 14's kill case alone.
    - Cases: `sender_delivers_only_to_its_siblings_session` (**[Revision 1]** addressed by the uds path of a listening
      sibling's pid; a non-sibling pid and a sibling not listening exit 1), `sender_runs_its_plugin_hooks_names_only`,
      `receiver_fires_the_cross_session_variant_once`, `receiver_reads_no_inbox_without_the_accept_settings`, and
      **[Revision 1]** `sender_refuses_an_address_not_of_the_uds_shape` (a bare session id, a relative dir, no
      `.sock` suffix: each exit 1, no hook run, no inbox file).

14. **The row's fake-agent cases** (`tests/cli_verify.rs`, over a test-built synthetic set at a test-owned version,
    `tests/support/verify.rs` gaining the `cross-session-1` framing shape named SYNTHETIC; committed nowhere):
    - `cross_session_prefix_reads_pass_over_the_fake_sender`: step line `[29/29] cross-session-prefix … pass`; the
      stamp's `cross_session_probe` reads `outcome` `harness`, `prefix` `cross-session`, `sender_tools` `["send"]`,
      `send_result` `delivered`; one `verify-sender` process pair; Run B's receipt argv carries `--settings` then the
      literal; the sender's argv carries `--plugin-dir` and no `--settings`; `/clear` is pasted after the turn. (That the
      names-only mode files no payload is proven at step 4, not here: the probe dir is gone when verify exits.)
      **[Revision 1]** The case also asserts the sender's `-p` prompt. It equals `CROSS_SESSION_SENDER_HEAD` +
      `uds:<the case's runtime dir>/cc-socks/<Run B's pid>.sock` + `CROSS_SESSION_SENDER_TAIL`, where Run B's pid is
      the one its receipt line records, and it holds no session id. The fake sender's receipt line records the prompt
      it was given (`tests/support/verify.rs`'s receipt reader). The case's verify runs under a test-owned, short,
      owner-only `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (the support's `SOCKET_ROOT_VAR` form, `tests/support/home.rs:625`).
    - **[Revision 1]** `cross_session_prefix_reads_not_run_without_a_runtime_dir`: verify runs with `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`
      removed from its env. The case asserts no `verify-sender` process pair, no sender receipt line, `outcome`
      `not-run`, `sender_tools` and `send_result` null, the row `fail`, and exit 1. Under fork X1 (b) the case
      instead pins the `/run/user/<euid>` composition.
    - **The keeps-its-red case** (`inputs#I1` item 8), ONE rstest
      `cross_session_prefix_keeps_its_red_under_the_accept_settings`, Run B's argv carrying the literal in both:
      `case_1_no_prompt_arrives` (the set holds no `cross-session-1`: the fake sender exits 1, outcome `sender-failed`)
      and `case_2_arrives_unprefixed` (the synthetic prompt opens with plain text, outcome `unprefixed`); each reads
      `fail`, exit 1. The sender-exits-0 `no-prompt` path is held at unit level (step 15): over the fake it would wait
      out the 30 s window past the 20 s kill (`(test-plan · decision/verify-driven-tests-20s-kill)`).
    - `cross_session_prefix_ends_run_b_by_kill_when_the_box_is_not_up`: no Ctrl-C byte after the turn, no `/clear`.

16. **Every relied-count literal moves to 29** — research's sweep, 94 hits in 9 files
    (`/28\]|28 pass|; 28\]|len\(\), 28|Some\("28"\)|\("rows", "28"\)`). `src/run/version_gate.rs` and
    `src/run/auto_verify.rs` tests step to 29. Each `cli_verify` summary literal moves by whether its Run B reaches
    step 11, read against its case's path, never re-counted to green. `tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs`'s
    `assert_framed_exit` (line 216) keys its expected failing lines on the variants a set holds: exit 0 only on a set
    holding both `question-permission` and `cross-session` variants; otherwise exactly the lines of the rows the set
    lacks read `fail`, the summary's fail count that number. As built (the stopped run's note 7): `src/run/auto_verify.rs`'s
    tests needed no edit, since they read `LedgerRow::relied()`, not a literal count.

title: C. The round: `XS-2` (`inputs#I8` item 2; `XS` fired red, its record `evidence/live-round.md`)

data.head: ### C. The round: `XS-2` (`inputs#I8` item 2; `XS` fired red, its record `evidence/live-round.md`)

body:
`XS` is base line 1 of `evidence/cross-starts.ndjson`. `XS-2` is base line 2 under `--cap 2 --spare 1`, in `XS`'s
shape (2.1.328 by path, the `VR` arm, the rig's scratch home and private config). The one change is the sender's `to`:
the composed uds address. The spare stays unspent: it covers a rig refusal before the ledger line, or a host CONTENDED
by a neighbour, never a red reading. A red `XS-2` stops implement, and a third base start is the operator's.

24. **Copy `target/live-rig/XS-2/record/2.1.328/` over `fixtures/claude/2.1.328/`**, a plain copy; the one new file joins
    (32 → 33, predicted: record what the copy measures) and `Mcp.tools-list-1.json` stays as committed.
    `evidence/landing.md` lists the files with sha256 prefixes before anything runs over the set; a file the hygiene
    suite refuses is a red, never scrubbed. `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs` walks the `cross-session` framing stem.
- `fixtures/claude/2.1.328/UserPromptSubmit.cross-session-1.json` — `XS-2`'s recorded cross-session arrival, through the scrub

- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — the 29th row, `tool_word`, `send_result_word`, `tool_capture_document`, `tool_file_name`, `ProbePlugin::Sender`, the sender texts, `uds_address` and its four compiled literals (Revision 1), `sender_prompt` over an address, `CROSS_SESSION_SETTINGS`, `cross_session_reading`, the measured block, `TypedRun.cross_session`, `framing_variants`
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases_checks.rs` — the row's pass and fail tables, the classifier tables, `uds_address_composes_the_cli_socket_name`, the sender prompt over an address
- `src/cmd/verify.rs` — `SENDER_DEADLINE`, the sender inputs, 29 step lines, the record's file, the one `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` read (Revision 1, held behind X1)
- `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` — `Inputs` gains the sender's cwd and dirs, and `runtime_dir`
- `src/cmd/verify/typed/turns.rs` — the cross-session turn gated on Run B's pid and the composed address, the sender spawn, its waits, its `Tool.*` read
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — the fake sender resolving its target by the uds address, its plugin hooks, the inbox receiver, the screen option
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/agents.rs` — the sibling check by pid and parent pid, in place of the registry lookup by session id
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/test_cases_modes.rs` — the five fake cases
- `tests/support/verify.rs` — the synthetic `cross-session-1` framing shape, named synthetic; the sender's receipt line carrying its prompt; a test-owned `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`
- `tests/cli_verify.rs` — the row's fake cases, the keeps-its-red case, the no-runtime-dir case, the sender prompt's address, counts, process-line lists
- `fixtures/claude/2.1.328/` — re-recorded whole by `XS-2`; `Mcp.tools-list-1.json` kept

The block runs in this order: phase A (formatter, linter, the agent crate's and the root bin's unit cases, the canary
binary, then the workspace unit, integration and E2E layers on 28 rows); phase B (formatter, linter, the agent crate,
the rig's library cases, the root bin, the row's `cli_verify` cases, the canary binary), then the four filtered control
entries; the round (entries 20–34, `round` and `live` entries ONLY, `inputs#I8` item 8). Its after-reads of other
actors' state are keyed to the round right after `XS-2`: `gate.py run --live-legs` fires them in its span, in block
order, and the wrap's light gate never re-fires them (`inputs#I3` item 3). Then come the census keyed `operator` and the
leg-less after-reads of `XS-2`'s own products, all after the span; then after the landing (`diff -r`, the three layers);
then the operator pass. **Revision 1:** entries 1–8 (phase A) are not re-fired; implement starts at entry 9 (step 18). What is not run, and why: no mutation run
(`inputs#I1` item 10); no release-check entry (CI's `release` job runs it); between phase B and the landing no
stamped-home suite runs (§Steps intro). Every test start runs under a test-owned home and user home; every waiting test
takes a bound under the 20 s lint. The live start runs under the rig's private scratch; the rig's `--deadline` bounds
it under the entry's `timeout`. The live leg's non-priming probes are the round entries ahead of it. `XS` and `XS-2` are
ledgered in `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-21-cross-session-prefix-ledger-row/evidence/cross-starts.ndjson`; `--cap` is
the running total of base lines in that one file (`XS` stands as line 1, so `XS-2` is `--cap 2`). The census after the
last live leg is keyed `operator` and stands after the span.

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries. Each fires on an
entry filtered to its guard's own cases (ids within 16 characters, `inputs#I3` items 1–2). It reads «holds» only when
its own case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line. Each filter selects 0 tests on the tree before its case exists and at
least one once it does. Revision 1 re-fires the three standing controls and adds `address-shape`:
| | `prefix-match` | `no-payload` | `unread-shape` | `address-shape` |
| **File** | `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` | `src/cmd/hook.rs` | `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` | `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` |

| **The edit removes** | the clause of `cross_session_reading` that reads `unprefixed` when `harness_prefix` is `None` | the payload guard inside `capture_names_only`: its `drop(bytes);` replaced by the `file_from(...)` filing (the case calls that function directly, testing.md 2026-09-25 ext. 2026-10-07; the stopped run's deviation 2) | the fall-through of `send_result_word` to `unread` (replaced by `refused`) | the byte-set refusal of `uds_address` (every byte accepted) |

| **Case** | `cross_session_prefix_fails_when::case_2_no_prefix` | `names_only_capture_files_closed_words_and_no_payload` | `send_result_word_reads_only_the_boolean::case_5_success_a_string` | `uds_address_composes_the_cli_socket_name::case_4_a_space` |
| **Fired on** | entry 16, `--timeout 300` | entry 17, `--timeout 600` | entry 18, `--timeout 300` | entry 19, `--timeout 300` |

body:
- (cross-session) `matrix#v2-25`: the prefix the CLI puts on a message another session sends in is the stamped relied
  row `cross-session-prefix`. Live on 2.1.328 in `XS-2` (`XS` read red, `evidence/live-round.md`): `cross-session-prefix:
  pass`, `cross-session: harness`, `pass-count: 29/29`, and its kept stamp `cross-stamp-2.json` at `29 ok`, the sender's
  `to` the uds address verify composed from Run B's child pid. Over the fake agent:
  `cross_session_prefix_reads_pass_over_the_fake_sender` in the phase B `cli_verify` entry; after the landing,
  `contract_ledger_probes` replays the recorded `UserPromptSubmit.cross-session-1.json` with 2.1.328 at
  `29 pass 0 fail` in the `run --e2e` entry. Under the accept literal the row keeps its red:
  `cross_session_prefix_keeps_its_red_under_the_accept_settings` reads `fail` when no prompt arrives and when it arrives
  unprefixed. A red start (`XS`, or a red `XS-2`) verifies nothing (`(test-plan · decision/live-failing-reading-not-verification)`;
  `(architecture · decision/harness-prompt-prefixes)`, `(security-plan · decision/harness-prefix-literals)`).

- (address) **[Revision 1]** verify composes Run B's address `uds:<runtime dir>/cc-socks/<pid>.sock` and the sender's
  prompt holds it and no session id: `uds_address_composes_the_cli_socket_name` (eight literal cases, the 103-byte CLI
  bound among them) and `sender_prompt_holds_the_address_between_its_compiled_parts` in the phase B agent-crate entry;
  the pass case's prompt assertion and `cross_session_prefix_reads_not_run_without_a_runtime_dir` in the phase B
  `cli_verify` entry; the fake sender's `sender_refuses_an_address_not_of_the_uds_shape`; the `address-shape` control
  reads «holds». No directory is read, listed or stat'ed by verify to compose it (step 11).
- (round) The whole round fires as ONE `gate.py run --live-legs` call: its dry-run reads no pre-flight refusal (P5).

- (live) `XS-2` reads green on its entry's atoms within the operator's cap (`--cap 2 --spare 1`); the after-reads hold:
  `29 ok`, `kept-stamps: unchanged` (HF, HG and XS's kept stamps) and `live-stamp: unmoved` (both round-keyed), the
  name diff at exactly 2 lines; the stale-socket counts before and after are a READING recorded in
  `evidence/live-round.md` (`inputs#I3` item 4).

- **Reading the user's other sessions or the registry to «check» the target** — reads viola does not own
  (`founder-forks.md` §3 of the take-up). **[Revision 1]** The socket address form, set aside there as «a read», is now
  the operator's chosen mend WITHOUT a read (`inputs#I8` item 1). Verify composes it and does not probe it: no `stat`,
  no listing, no symlink test, nothing read of `cc-socks/`, the roster or the peer key (`inputs#I8` items 3, 5).

- **[Revision 1] Addressing Run B by a NAME, with or without a `ListAgents` call; dropping the row** — declined by the
  operator (`inputs#I8` item 1; `red-analysis.md` §C (ii), (iii)).

- **[Revision 1] A diagnostic start on the unmended sender; reading the gate's cached flag; a `to-shape` word** — not
  chosen (`red-analysis.md` §B, §C (i)); the mend changes the address only.

- **A retry of the sender inside one verify; a base start beyond `XS-2`** — `inputs#I8` item 2: a red `XS-2` stops
  implement, and a third base start is the operator's.

- **The cause table** (`inputs#I2` item 8), read off the start's `cross_session_probe` when `outcome` is `no-prompt`
  (the take-up's `founder-forks.md` §1 names C1–C5). **[Revision 1]** Extended for the uds form (`inputs#I8` item 4;
  `red-analysis.md` §D1), the table `XS-2` is read against. With a `uds:` `to`, C4, the name resolution, cannot occur:
  the tool's uds branch sends straight to the path with no roster lookup.

  | `sender_tools` | `send_result` | Reads (uds `to`) | Named or AMBIGUOUS |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | holds `send` | `none` | the send fired no PostToolUse: refused at input validation. The tool's `validateInput` refuses a uds `to` when the cross-session gate is off (C2), before the tool runs. Whether `validateInput` also refuses a path form is unread | AMBIGUOUS: C2, or the composed path refused at input; the gate is the one the bundle shows |
  | holds `send` | `refused` | a THROWN send: the path form wrong for this CLI (a non-local path, a symlink at the path); the socket gone (Run B ended, or a CLI that names its socket otherwise, so no file at the composed path); the 5 s connect timeout; the inbox rate limit (`paced`) | AMBIGUOUS among the four; C2 excluded (it refuses at input, row above), C4 excluded (no resolution) |
  | holds `send` | `delivered` | the tool reported success, and no prompt arrived in 30 s: the RECEIVE side, i.e. the peer key missing (a frame sent with no token; whether Run B drops it is unread), Run B's startup hold, or the CLI's receive kill switch | AMBIGUOUS among the three; not split from a late arrival past the window (`latency_ms` null) |
  | holds `send` | `unread` | the result's shape unmeasured | AMBIGUOUS across every row above |
  | holds `search`, no `send` | — | C1: the fetch path ran and the model did not send | named; C3 not excluded (the fetch's result is not read) |
  | no `send`, no `search` | — | C1 or C3 | AMBIGUOUS: not offered inline and not fetched, or offered and not called |
  | `none` (no file) | — | no tool called at all, or the plugin's hooks did not run | AMBIGUOUS; a plugin not run is a finding of its own |

  `outcome` `not-run` with a sender never started (both words `null`) is «no address composed» or «no pid» (step 11).

its evidence dir from disk first. This directive is the only file of its folder you read or snap.

**In your own chat messages never print a compiled screen literal verbatim**: name it. This session is driven
through the pinned product, which holds none of the last five mends: call no scheduled-wake or timer tool.

  `viola verify --record` of the 29-row tree, with the print-mode sender (`claude -p` on Haiku, its one allowed
  tool the CLI's own send, its capture plugin in the names-only mode, its target the uds address verify composes for Run B) beside Run B; only verify's compiled pastes
  are typed; NO key and NO byte into any CLI dialog; a held-message approval in Run B is never answered; the
  kept stamp and the record stay under `target/live-rig/`.
- **No start follows `XS-2`:** a third base start is the operator's, through the phase's
  revision door. **A RED `XS-2` of any cause stops implement before the landing; no start follows it.** The spare is
  spent only on a start the rig refuses before its ledger line or a host CONTENDED by a neighbour — never on a
  red reading; the model's run-to-run variance is a spend the overseer names, not this run.
- **Nothing is written under the real `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola`.** `~/.claude/.credentials.json` is READ once by
  the rig (a 0600 copy, removed on every exit path). `~/.viola/ledger/stamps.json` is read for its sha alone,
  RE-TAKEN right before `XS-2`, and must read unmoved right after it. The pinned product is not rebuilt, replaced or
  re-pinned. This session runs claude 2.1.330; the start goes against 2.1.328 by path.
- **The sender's capture writes closed words only:** no payload, no argument, no model text reaches any file,
  stamp, fixture, log or message of yours. `sender-tools` and `send-result` are READINGS, never atoms.
- **The composed address is never probed by verify and never printed:** no value of `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and no
  composed path in your messages, a log, the stamp or a fixture — names and closed words only.

- Run nothing heavier than this chunk's own gate entries. Read `df` before any step that rebuilds whole.

- A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop and say so. On an account-limit
  refusal, stop where you are. Remove no scratch clone by a recursive delete: name it in the report.

a stamp holding exactly the seventeen ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row holds, or exactly the eighteen ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows holds, or exactly the twenty-one ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows holds, or exactly the twenty-two ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board holds, or exactly the twenty-three ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row holds, all `pass`, reads unverified; so every home stamped before chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row reads `cli_verified:false` until its next `viola verify`); `scrub`, `is_clean` (reads through `unclean`), `signature_rows`, `screen_is_clean`, `screen_fault` → `ScreenFault { row, seam, why }`, `unclean` → the closed `Unclean` codes `home-path` · `absolute-path` · `username` · `email`. `verified` returns `Result<bool, AgentError>`: a wrong-shaped envelope is `AgentError::StampsMalformed` ("the capability stamps are malformed"). `AgentError` sits at the crate root and also holds `resolve_program`'s one refusal, `ProgramNotFound`, with a fixed message (arch [Error Handling]). `resolve_program` returns `Result<PathBuf, AgentError>`, in the crate and in the root wrapper `src/run/mod.rs`.

The `viola` binary. It holds the clap 4.6.7 dispatch (`src/main.rs`, one module per subcommand in `src/cmd/`) and the `run` wrapper (`src/run/`): the PTY pump, the wheel, the readiness-gate wiring and the channel server dispatch. It also owns the pinned copy + plugin write-out, the obs init (`viola::obs`: `MillisUtc`, `viola_obs_init`, the panic hook, the detail writer, the catch-site reporter `report_internal_error`; `open_role_file` and `write_detail` run `strict::check_diagnostics` on an existing `diagnostics/` folder and on the role or detail file before `ensure_private_dir` narrows anything — a symbolic link refused, a folder to the read rule, a file to the read rule, an absent path passing — and a refusal is a failed open: the writer ends at `std::io::sink`, a detail line is dropped) and the human/`--json` output modules (the `human` module: `src/human.rs`, with its phases under `src/human/` — mirror, escape, board, style (the colour layer: `Depth`, `Tokens`, `Facts`, `decide`, `read`), wait, verbs, hints —; `src/human.rs` holds the stderr refusal writer `write_refusal` behind `refuse`, the stderr `write_internal_error` (`error: internal error\n`) behind `internal_error`, and the stdout `write_result` behind `result`, each one `write_all`; called by `run`, `revive`, `verify`, `send`, `wait`, `last`, `list`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `plugin install` and the `main` catch site; no print macro, no `#[allow]`). `viola verify` (`src/cmd/verify.rs`) drives the one print-mode probe and then the six interactive PTY runs, with one print-mode sender, `verify-sender`, inside Run B's cross-session turn (`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` and its children under `src/cmd/verify/typed/`: Run A untrusted in an OS-temp dir, Run B trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/` with compiled pastes — the probe prompt, then the long text, the tag-like text, the newline text (`PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE`, 113 bytes, one inner LF), `/compact` (`PROBE_COMPACT_COMMAND`), `/clear` and `/mcp disable viola-probe-absent` (the `local-command-echo` row's probe, passing on a new stdout tag with no UserPromptSubmit within the confirmation window; with no readable transcript the paste skipped and the row failing), then eighth `/context` (the relied `local-command-context` row's probe, passing on a new stdout tag with no UserPromptSubmit within the confirmation window; a failing read of it is `fail`, never `absent`), each added one only into a settled input box, waited for after an added text turn and after the `/compact` turn up to `PROBE_DEADLINE` (`box_wait`: 2.1.287 shows a paste hint in the input-box literal's place for 8.0 s after a long paste) — and, once its first turn has settled and before its framing pastes, ONE `claude agents --json` read (`typed::turns::agents_read`: Run B's program, cwd the probe dir, the R8 strip, `VERSION_DEADLINE`, none once a stop is read; its capture kept in memory, never written to the captures dir; no live start added; in CI the fake agent's `agents` mode answers it), Run C's dialogs in `-dialogs/`, Run D's plan in `-plan/`, then Run E trusted in `-resume/`, resuming Run B's first session with `--resume <id>` (`viola_agent_claude::resume_args(id, false)`, the id Run B's first SessionStart `session_id` through `ledger::resume_target`; empty input, no `--settings`, ended by a kill), then last Run F, after Run E, starting in an untrusted folder for which verify wrote a trust record (the `trust-record` row passing only when the record was written, Run A showed the trust modal, and Run F's start shows no modal and the input box; verify writes that record for its own temp folder only into the Claude config file its child reads, located through `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` only when `claude_env_keep` keeps it, never creating an absent file, and removes that one record after; `run`'s and `revive`'s start, on a verified CLI, write the trust record of an untrusted spawn folder); no key into any dialog — the hidden `hook --capture --answers` arm in `src/cmd/hook.rs` answers C and D's from `PROBE_ANSWERS`), checks the relied ledger rows (`check_rows` walks `LedgerRow::relied()`: every row of `LedgerRow::ALL` on every build, the relied `local-command-echo` among them; the relied cross-session-prefix row passing only when the print-mode sender's message to Run B, started with the crossSessionInbound accept settings, arrives opening with the CLI's cross-session harness prefix, else failing, never on the sender's words; the relied identity-floor row passing when every CLAUDE name the CLI adds to a SessionStart hook, kept names dropped first, is an identity-floor or known non-identity name, and failing on an unknown name or an unread or off-shape env-names file), prints the step lines (each `pass`, `absent` or `fail`) and `stamped` summary (its pass count including an absent `browser-tools-prompt`, the one relied row whose `absent` counts toward verified) and writes the stamps through `viola_state::stamps::update_stamps` (its `StampsError::StrictModes` refusal printing the home-state pair, exit 1); before its `cli` log opens it runs `viola_state::strict::check_home_tree(home, None, None)` (the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/`, each that exists), a refusal printing the home pair and exiting 1 with no step line, no summary and no line; a verify stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (`cmd::verify::stop`: `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`, installed by `viola verify` alone, its handler only setting one process-global flag that every wait of the run reads) kills and reaps the running child with no key, starts no later run, writes no stamp and exits 1 (`unable: verify was stopped before it finished` / `hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI`, stdout empty), its drop guards removing only the dirs, and its own trust record from the Claude config file, that run created; SIGKILL, a crash and a failed handler install keep the OS default and leave the dirs to be removed by hand; `run::version_gate` reads them at `run` start. The panic detail backtrace is raw, never-symbolised frames (`src/panic_frames.rs`). It is the only crate with anyhow (dispatch edge and the catch-site reporter) and tracing-subscriber, and it consumes only normalised events.

- `hook <event> --capture <DIR>` (hidden) is `verify`'s capture arm: no `VIOLA_*` and no environment value read, no obs init, no channel; with the hidden `--names-only` (valid only with `--capture`) only owner-only `Tool.<k>.json` files of closed tool and send-result words, never a payload byte; without it a raw 0600 write (on SessionStart alone also `Env.<k>.json` owner-only beside the payload: the CLAUDE names of its own process, every other name only counted, no value ever read or written), exit 0 always.

- `viola verify [--record <dir>] [-- <program> [args…]]` — drive one print-mode probe (Haiku) and six interactive PTY runs (Run A untrusted in an OS-temp dir, Run B trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/` with compiled pastes (the probe prompt, a long text, a tag-like text, a text holding one inner LF, `/compact`, `/clear`, then `/mcp disable viola-probe-absent`, the local-command-echo row's probe, skipped with that row failed when no transcript is readable, then `/context`, the local-command-context row's probe, a failing read of it `fail`, never `absent`) and one `claude agents --json` read once its first turn has settled, before the added pastes (held in memory, spawn pair `agents-probe`, no start added; in CI the fake agent's `agents` mode answers it) and one print-mode sender, `verify-sender`, inside Run B's cross-session turn (Run B started with the crossSessionInbound accept settings, the sender addressing it by `uds:<runtime>/cc-socks/<pid>.sock`, never a bare session id; the cross-session-prefix row passes only when the message arrives opening with the CLI's cross-session harness prefix, else fails; no runtime dir runs no turn), Run C's dialogs in `-dialogs/`, Run D's plan in `-plan/`, then Run E in `-resume/` resuming Run B's first session with `--resume <id>` (input empty, no `--settings`), then Run F in an untrusted temp folder whose trust record verify writes into the Claude config file its child reads (never creating an absent file; a run or revive start writes a record only for its own untrusted spawn folder, on a verified CLI), passing the trust-record row only when the record was written, Run A showed the trust modal and Run F's start shows no modal and the input box; no key into any dialog — the probe hook answers C and D's) against the CLI (default `claude`), check the relied ledger rows (`LedgerRow::relied()`, on every build), print `[NN/MM]` step lines ending `pass`, `absent` or `fail` (`absent` on the browser-tools-prompt row alone, when no run met the CLI's browser-tools prompt; `MM` the relied count; the last `[MM/MM] browser-tools-prompt …`) + the `stamped <ver>  <n> pass  <m> fail` summary on stdout (`<n>` counting every relied row that counts toward verified, an absent browser-tools-prompt among them) and write `ledger/stamps.json`; exit 1 on a failing row; exit 1 with the home-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, no step line, no summary and no log line when `check_home_tree` refuses its home, `ledger/`, `bin/` or `plugin/` before its `cli` log opens (and the same pair, exit 1, after the step lines, when `update_stamps` refuses `ledger/stamps.json`, with `detail:"strict-modes-failed"` on its `process-exit` under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`); a run stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM kills its child with no key, removes only the probe dirs it created and its own trust record from the Claude config file, writes no stamp, leaves stdout empty, prints `unable: verify was stopped before it finished` / `hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI` and exits 1 (SIGKILL, a crash or a failed handler install leaves the dirs to remove by hand). `--record <dir>` also writes the scrubbed `<dir>/<ver>/<Event>.default.json` fixtures, the `<Event>.<stem>-<n>.json` dialog variants, Run B's `paste-<n>` / `compact-<n>` / `clear-<n>` framing variants, Run E's first SessionStart as `SessionStart.resume-1.json`, Run B's agents read as `Agents.recorded-1.json` (Run B's own row only), the env-names fixture `Env.recorded-1.json` (names only, never a value: `v` 1 plus `added`) and signature-only `Screen.<phase>.json` screens (a footer or modal row whole, the input box's rule row as its rule chars alone and its prompt row as the prompt char alone, every other row empty; a box whose live prompt row holds a home path, the username or an email refuses the recording) when 0 rows fail; an unclean recording is refused naming the file and check code. A hidden `--record-first-screens`, absent from `--help` and passed only by the live rig, makes a failed `--record` verify write a first-screen file of whole scrubbed rows per run short of the input box (Run A's trust excepted), refused whole when unclean, kept locally and never committed. Run it from a folder you trust in Claude Code whose external CLAUDE.md import is answered. Against the real CLI: local only, spends tokens; CI runs it only against the fake agent's `-p/--print` mode and its `--screens --turn-stop --trusted-root --dialogs --framing --transcript --trust-config` interactive modes, under a test-owned user home whose config file is seeded empty and owner-only and named to the fake agent by `--trust-config`, with a short owner-only runtime dir (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`) the test owns for the stamp's life (every stamping verify passes `--transcript` beside `--framing`, or Run B's echo probe is skipped and the local-command-echo row fails). The `Mcp.<variant>.json` MCP exchanges are recorded not by `--record` but by the test-only `viola-mcp-tap` (`record` / `fixture`, the same scrub and closed refusal codes; architecture §Occupied Resources → Binary); the recorded Hyprland replies likewise by the test-only `viola-hypr-tap`, under the same scrub

- Stamps file: `ledger/stamps.json` in the Ledger stamps envelope `{"v":1,"written_at","writer":"verify","data":{"versions":{"<ver>":{"verified_at","rows":{…},"measured":{…}}}}}` (arch §Standard Contracts; `measured.env_probe` holds the identity-floor probe's `read`, `added`, `unknown`, `other_count` and `unshaped`, names only, every kept name removed; `measured.cross_session_probe` holds the cross-session probe's `outcome`, `prefix`, `latency_ms`, `sender_tools` and `send_result`, closed words and one number); a version is verified only when its stamp holds every relied row (`LedgerRow::relied()`, on every build) `pass`, or `absent` on `browser-tools-prompt` alone: a seventeen-row stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row reads unverified (`cli_verified:false`) until the next `viola verify`, and so does an eighteen-row stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows, a twenty-one-row stamp written before chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows, a twenty-two-row stamp written before chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board , a twenty-three-row stamp written before chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row or a twenty-two-row stamp written before chunk 2026-11-17-trust-record-ledger-row; a stamp's `rows` maps each row id to `pass` or `fail`, browser-tools-prompt may also read `absent`, and trust-record holds the trust writer's code word instead when no record was written

- `boot [--session <id>] [--instance <name>[:<args>]]... [--unstamped] [--cli-version <ver>] [--agents-mode recorded|oversize|malformed]` — build, create a home, stamp via `viola verify` against the fake agent (with a short owner-only runtime dir the harness owns for the stamp's life), start wrappers (a stamped session's under a session user home seeded with an empty config), wait for readiness (`--agents-mode` (default `recorded`, an unknown value usage `arguments`) writes the fake agent's `agents-mode` file (0600) beside the session's `bin/claude` copy after the stamp and before `supervise.json`, setting no env var, and is recorded as `agents_mode` in `session.json` and `supervise.json`)

- Modes built: `--suppress-prompt-submit`, `--local-command-mode`, `--inject-harness-turn`, `--exit-no-eof` (its re-exec mode `--hold-stdout-internal`, which sleeps 10 s and writes nothing, is also spawned directly by the server-identity impostor cases, `tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs` and `tests/hook_fail_open.rs`, as the live process their snapshot records, reaped by each file's `Held` `Drop` guard), `--report-version`, `--trim-prompt-end` (a bracketed paste plus Enter fires UserPromptSubmit with its trailing run of space, TAB, CR and LF removed), `--framing` (verify's Run B: a compiled paste text fires its recorded `paste-<n>` variant unchanged, the probed `/clear` its recorded `clear-<n>` SessionEnd then SessionStart and no UserPromptSubmit, and the probed `/compact` the recorded `SessionStart.compact-1` with the last fired SessionStart's `session_id` and no UserPromptSubmit), the capped test-only hold `--paste-hint-ms` (10 s at most: a cleared screen after the long paste's turn), the test-only screen switch `--tag-turn-screen <phase>` (with `--framing` and `--turn-stop`: `Screen.<phase>` of the set after the tag-like paste's turn alone, in place of `Screen.turn`), the test-only screen switch `--long-turn-screen <phase>` (with `--framing` and `--turn-stop`: `Screen.<phase>` of the set after the long paste's turn alone, after its Stop, in place of `Screen.turn`), `--vt100-panic-bytes` (after its `start` receipt it writes `e4 b8 ad` once to its terminal; under a 24×1 PTY that panics vt100's feed), `--start-screen <phase>` (under `--screens`, a trusted start draws `Screen.<phase>` in place of its ready screen and keeps it standing; each stdin byte is one `key` receipt line, Ctrl-C ends it with no key line, and no byte reaches the input box). `--transcript` (argv-only) creates `<exe dir>/transcripts/` at 0700 at start and gives the launch SessionStart a `transcript_path` to a seeded 0600 file named by its session id (replayed framing variants not rewritten; a test that must have no transcript removes none from the shared build, it runs its own private copy of the fake agent in a test-owned directory); under `--local-command-mode` a submitted local command whose post-condition is the stdout tag, and under `--framing` the exact verify echo probe command or the exact `/context` probe command, append one stdout tag line to the last started session's transcript and fire no hook. `--settings <file>` is accepted; the fake agent reads its cross-session inbox only when the value holds the accept settings, and otherwise ignores it (its cross-session sender resolves its target by the uds socket address alone, delivers only to its sibling and refuses an address not of the uds shape). Beside `--turn-stop`, `--turn-fail <variant>` ends the turn with the recorded set's `StopFailure.<variant>` payload in place of `Stop.default`. `--trust-config <file>` reads trust from that config file by the CLI's walk (the canonical cwd's exact key, then each parent up to the git root, so inside a repository the cwd's own record counts) through a bounded read; any failure reads untrusted. Under `--screens` with an untrusted cwd it draws claude 2.1.325's unnumbered trust form over the set's recorded modal (selector first on No, directly above the recorded trust row, row 16 with no recorded modal); arrows move the selector, Enter on No exits 1, and the launch SessionStart fires only after Enter on the trust row, which draws the ready screen. Built for `viola revive`'s tests and, under the fake agent, verify's Run E: `--resume <id>` (the launch SessionStart reports source `resume` and that id) and `--fork-session` (beside `--resume`, the compiled fork id; alone it changes nothing); and the capped test-only hold `--stop-receipt-hold-ms` (1 000 ms at most, holding the Stop hook's receipt to force a race window open), and the test-only hold `--trust-record-blank` (a start trusted by the trust record alone draws no screen, holding verify's Run F window open for a stop case). Built: the mode word `agents` (a first word `agents` answers `agents --json` from files beside its exe: `agents-mode` (`recorded` · `oversize` · `malformed`, absent = `recorded`), `agents-rows.json` (planted rows) and the live `sessions/<pid>.json` registry, a row written just before its launch SessionStart fires, a dead or reused pid skipped through one `viola_state::liveness::start_times()` read; built on the recorded `Agents.recorded-1.json`; no option and no env added). Exits on `\x03` or at stdin EOF, and exits 1 on Enter on the trust form's No, first waiting for a hook still running and starting no other; on Unix every command it spawns (each hook) runs in a process group of its own (`process_group(0)`, as the `--exit-no-eof` holder does), because a hangup of its PTY's foreground group, at its exit as session leader or when a killed wrapper closes the PTY, cuts a `viola hook` short in its exit-time coverage write (a cut-short profile, measured); the agent itself, its PTY's session leader, cannot leave that group (`setpgid` refuses a leader), so on Unix its exit ignores SIGHUP from its first step (`\x03` or stdin's end): a hangup that lands while it exits (a killed wrapper, or portable-pty's SIGHUP-first kill) no longer cuts its own exit-time coverage write, and one that lands before the exit begins still ends it (measured). That exit, shared Unix code, is witnessed on Linux only: `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs` `fake_agent_exit_outlives_a_hangup_that_lands_while_it_exits` (`cfg(target_os = "linux")`) reads the SIGHUP disposition through `ps -o sigignore= -p <pid>`; it runs on CI's one leg, `ubuntu-latest`.

- Root fixture chain: `tests/support/` (`home` → `fake_agent_path` → `stamped_home`, a copy, never a link, of one `viola verify` stamp per build (taken against the fake agent at the recorded `DEFAULT_CLI_VERSION` over `fixtures/claude` under a test-owned user home whose config file is seeded empty and owner-only and a short owner-only runtime dir the test owns for the stamp's life, the fake agent told that config file (a `--record` verify keeps the real HOME and points a kept `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at the test-owned user home instead), the fake agent given `--transcript` beside `--framing`, once per pair of built binaries, under an exclusive lock, kept under `target/e2e-home` keyed by the binaries' hashes) → `booted_wrapper`; `StampedHome::unstamped` for the unverified path; every long-lived viola child a root test spawns is tied to its spawning test thread by a parent-death kill (spawned only on a thread that outlives it; exiting when its recorded parent is already gone; `cross_killed_test_census_finds_no_untied_viola_spawn` finds no untied viola spawn in any test source; `every_test_verify_runs_under_a_test_home` holds every test-started `viola verify` start tied to a test-owned home, and every test-started `viola run` and `viola revive` runs under a test-owned user home, never the runner's real HOME, with a closed exempt list whose every entry carries its reason, proven red on a planted untied start), so a killed or panicked test leaves no wrapper or fake agent, and a Drop guard that kills, then waits, still covers the normal end; `Wrapper::stop` waits for the endpoint to be unconnectable, not only the exit; `wait_ready` at its deadline appends the stalled wrapper's state — its last `run-<name>.ndjson` event, its `/proc/<pid>/wchan` and the `stat` state field (`note_stall`) — to the watch report before the panic, signalling nothing and adding nothing to a passing boot). Homes live under `target/e2e-home/viola-test-*` (the base prepared by `prepare_home_base` under the harness keeper's contract; on the Linux dev host it is a link to an owner-only tmpfs directory, so removals reach outside the working directory and a kept home does not survive a reboot), kept per `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES` / `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED` (viola-e2e's booted lifecycle tests: a `Booted` drop guard stops the session, then keeps the home only for a panicking test under `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1`); each records `owner.json` `{pid, started_at}`, and a new home (no keep flag set) first removes only dirs whose recorded owner process is gone — never by age or name, never a dir without a record, save a build's verify stamp dir, which carries none: another build's stamp is swept only when its lock is taken without waiting (a runner-killed test never drops its home); the drop and that sweep both go through `remove_owned`, which deletes `owner.json` last, so a removal that stops part-way keeps the record. The chain exists once, as the sync root copy in `tests/support/`: viola-e2e has no copy and boots its sessions through its own `harness_session`; Path 1's flow lands on the root chain as `tests/path1_run_start.rs`.

- It must not drift from the recorded `viola verify` fixtures, the spine, the dialog variants, the framing variants (`paste-<n>`, `compact-<n>`, `clear-<n>`) and the resume variant (`SessionStart.resume-1.json`, by `fake_agent_resume_replay_matches_every_recorded_resume_set`) and the compact variant (`SessionStart.compact-1.json`, once resumed into its own session, by `fake_agent_compact_replay_matches_every_recorded_compact_set`), which `contract_fake_agent_drift` replays byte for byte (contract suite; a hook whose payload names the send tool is left out of the dialog tier, so a side sender's hooks shift no position, every other dialog-tier hook still compared by position, event and bytes); it also compares the key and type shape of the fake agent's `agents` rows with each recorded `Agents.*.json` set (`fake_agent_agents_replay_matches_every_recorded_agents_set`).

- No per-byte or per-line logging in hot loops (PTY pump); no line per heartbeat tick — transitions only. The Hyprland seam writes one `process-start` / `process-exit{subject:"hyprctl-probe"}` pair around each hyprctl spawn, at viola's call site. A `viola run` start that spawns its automatic `viola verify` child writes one `process-start` / `process-exit{subject:"auto-verify"}` pair to the run log, the exit carrying `child_exit_status` and `duration_ms`. `viola verify`'s print-mode claude sender of Run B's cross-session turn writes one `process-start` / `process-exit{subject:"verify-sender"}` pair; its prompt and the composed socket address appear in no line.
